transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I guess what brings me in is... I just can't seem to shake this really heavy mix of fear and guilt lately. It's like I'm just tense all day, waiting for something else to go wrong. And I just keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened.
Did something traumatic happen before you started feeling this way?
Yeah, it did. Um... this has been going on for about four months now, ever since my husband had a bad fall during the porch repair.
Do unwanted memories of your husband’s fall keep popping into your mind?

Yeah, they do. Um... especially since I work around that kind of stuff. I'll just be at work, measuring a railing or maybe just hearing a ladder scrape against a wall, and out of nowhere I can see him falling. It's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just drops and my hands get all shaky.
Have you been avoiding things that remind you of your husband’s fall?

Yeah, I have. Um... I've actually started turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks. I just can't really do them right now. And even at home, I just... I find excuses not to talk about the repair. I don't even look at the spot where it happened. I just try to stay away from it.
Have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled since the fall?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean... I don't feel jumpy or constantly on edge or anything. It's really just when I'm around those specific things at work or the porch that I get upset. But in general, no, I wouldn't say I'm easily startled.
Since the fall, have you felt cut off or detached from other people?

No, not really. I mean, I still talk to my friends and my family just like I always have. I don't feel disconnected from them or anything. It's really just the stuff related to the accident that bothers me.
Since the fall, have you been feeling that what happened was your fault?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I do building inspections for a living, so... I keep thinking that if I missed something that important at my own house, then maybe I'm not as careful or competent as I thought I was. I know my work reports don't show that I'm doing a bad job or missing things, but... I just feel like I really should have caught it.
When your husband fell, did you actually see the fall happen?
No, I didn't see it actually happen. I was inside the house when the railing broke. I just heard the crash and... and then I ran out and saw him on the ground.
Since your husband’s fall, have you had nightmares about it?

Yeah, I have. Most nights I just lie there in bed for an hour or two, just... replaying everything in my head. And even when I finally do fall asleep, I'm waking up at every little creak the house makes. Or I wake up from these dreams where I just keep hearing the sound of him hitting the ground over and over again.
Since your husband’s fall, have you found it hard to feel positive emotions, like happiness or love?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, things have been stressful, obviously, but... I still feel happy when good things happen, and I still love my husband just as much as I always have. It's just... the anxiety about the accident that's the problem, not really my other emotions.
After the fall, did your husband’s injuries put his life in danger?
No, it wasn't life-threatening. He broke his arm and had a concussion, which was scary enough, but... the doctors said he wasn't in any real danger of dying. It was just a really bad break.
